title: Heterogeneity-Aware GPU Interconnect
one_line: Can capability-matched routing improve communication overhead for GPU made of deliberately non-uniform participants?
core_question: Can capability-matched routing improve communication overhead for GPU made of deliberately non-uniform participants?
research_problem: Design a new advanced GPU architecture
subject: GPU

facet.label: Interconnect
facet.assumed_limitation: Every additional participant increases the number of links that must be kept coherent, so coordination cost grows faster than the work added.

concept.name: Heterogeneity awareness
concept.description: Treat non-uniform participants as exploitable structure instead of averaging them away.
mechanism_steps: Characterise how the participants of {subject} actually differ
Derive which work type each participant class does best
Route each work type toward its best-matching class
Track the per-class queue the routing creates
Rebalance when one class becomes the bottleneck
Re-measure the characterisation, which changes under load
concept.core_question: Can capability-matched routing improve {metric} for {subject} made of deliberately non-uniform participants?
uncertainties: Stability of the capability profiles under real load
Whether matching overhead outweighs the placement gain
Tail behaviour when one class is starved

inspiration.display: ecology / niche partitioning + statistics + scheduling theory

why_interesting: The problem's 'Interconnect' dimension (how components exchange information) is where the conventional approach carries a structural assumption: Every additional participant increases the number of links that must be kept coherent, so coordination cost grows faster than the work added. AARL took a mechanism that already works in ecology / niche partitioning, statistics, scheduling theory - Treat non-uniform participants as exploitable structure instead of averaging them away. - and asked what happens if it is applied to GPU. If the mechanism transfers, the gain would come from removing that assumption rather than from tuning the existing design. Whether it transfers is exactly what is not established here.

gaps.question: The only result available for this direction is an ASSUMPTION-BASED RESULT driven by assumed multipliers (lr). What measured data would replace those assumptions?
gaps.why_it_matters: Until the multipliers are replaced by measurements, no claim about the mechanism's effect on communication overhead can be supported.
gaps.how_to_start: Instrument a representative workload and measure the multipliers directly, then re-run the same comparison.

gaps.question: How far does the recorded effect on communication overhead extend before it reverses? Only 3 configuration(s) were tested.
gaps.why_it_matters: A single operating point cannot show where the benefit ends.
gaps.how_to_start: Sweep the parameter that the mechanism acts on and record communication overhead at each point.

gaps.question: How does communication overhead scale as the number of interconnect participants grows beyond the tested range?
gaps.why_it_matters: Coordination mechanisms usually show their real cost only once the participant count grows.
gaps.how_to_start: Repeat the comparison at several participant counts and fit the curve.

first_experiment.objective: Establish whether the mechanism moves communication overhead for GPU at all, before tuning anything.
first_experiment.design: Baseline A: the conventional interconnect approach. Variant B: the Heterogeneity awareness mechanism applied only to the interconnect dimension. Keep every other parameter identical and use the same seed/warm-up.
first_experiment.decision_rule: Only claim support if B moves communication overhead outside the run-to-run spread of A; if the spread is larger than the effect, report INCONCLUSIVE rather than a direction.
first_experiment.what_would_make_it_stop: If A is already at the physical or structural limit of communication overhead, the comparison cannot discriminate and the design must change.
